A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GABAR research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support comparison. v2 has no appendix; v3 includes readable Appendices A.1-A.3.

before.justification: v2 Table 1 reports original planning experiments evaluating GABAR and its global-node ablation across six domains.

after.justification: v3 Tables 2 and 4 report original experiments across eight domains, including comparisons with other planners and multiple architectural ablations.

M1.justification: The reported decoder scoring rule changes from an MLP applied to concatenated hidden and candidate representations in v2 to an MLP applied to their elementwise product in v3 Algorithm 1. The graph encoder, supervised loss, sequential GRU decoding, beam search, and cycle avoidance remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds Spanner and Rovers to the six retained planning domains. These introduce tool-collection and nut-tightening tasks, and coordination of rovers with different capabilities, substantially broadening the evaluated planning requirements.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds evaluated comparisons with GPL, ASNets, and GRAPL, including on the six previously evaluated domains. v2 compared GABAR only with its global-node ablation and used Fast Downward as the plan-quality reference. The global-node ablation and Fast Downward reference are retained.

E3.justification: v2 evaluates 50 or 100 test problems per domain without difficulty breakdowns. v3 introduces easy, medium, and hard subsets containing 100 problems each, with explicit size allocations. It also removes mean and median plan length as evaluation metrics, retaining coverage and plan-quality ratio under the same 1000-step limit and Fast Downward reference.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained global-node ablation, v3 adds tests removing action representations, conditional decoding, and action ranking separately, plus a joint action-representation/conditional-decoding ablation. Tables 2 and 4 therefore investigate several previously untested component contributions across difficulty levels.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v3's combined-domain averages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 replaces the undivided per-domain results with extensive difficulty-specific results and removes the mean/median plan-length entries. For example, Table 2 newly reports hard Blocks coverage of 100% for GABAR, 10% for GPL, 92% for ASNets, and 38% for GRAPL. The revised test design prevents interpreting these as same-setting improvements over v2.

T1.justification: The decoder score's mathematical definition changes from concatenation-based to elementwise-product-based scoring. The planning definitions, state-transition formalism, graph feature definitions, and encoder update equations otherwise persist. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 primarily claims generalization from small training problems to larger instances. v3 additionally claims superiority over value-function and action-ranking baselines and greater sample efficiency. Its conclusion introduces the specific claim that GABAR needs only 25% of GPL's training data.

C2.justification: v3 develops substantial new explanations linking comparative performance to local versus globally consistent learning, conditional parameter dependencies, and explicit action-object representations. It attributes performance to the combination of these components. The earlier global-node interpretation and limitation concerning graph growth with high arity are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents hidden dimension 64, RTX 3080 hardware, training times of 1-2 hours per domain, beam width 2, and per-domain training-example counts. Algorithms 1-2 expand implementation documentation. Appendix A.1 also adds a code link and states that the dataset was submitted as supplementary material; these disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against earlier direct-action and relational-policy approaches, including works by Garg and colleagues, Janisch and colleagues, and Karia and Srivastava. It distinguishes GABAR through explicit action information and conditional decoding, extending v2's emphasis on value learning and state ranking.

P1.justification: The title and GABAR expansion change, substantial introductory and decoder passages are rewritten, and the results discussion is reorganized around baseline and component comparisons. Domain descriptions and the global-node analysis move into a new appendix structure, while encoder and decoder explanations are organized around pseudocode.

P2.justification: v3 changes the two-column format to a single-column layout, redraws Figure 1, and adds the worked graph-construction Figure 2. It introduces two algorithm listings and four tables, including dataset information and color-coded domain-by-difficulty result matrices, replacing v2's single compact results table.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses v2's limited comparative validation through three external baselines and targeted tests of the principal architectural components. Difficulty-specific evaluation and implementation disclosures substantially strengthen assessment of the approach. Reporting problems qualify this gain: hard Logistics coverage is 71% in Table 2 but 62% in parts of the discussion, and the claimed 25% training-data requirement lacks accompanying GPL budget evidence. These issues limit particular quantitative claims without eliminating the substantial improvement in validation.
